I nudge slightly above the market price to account for resolution-criteria ambiguity (a Zelensky-style political concession could be read as 'publicly agree') and for the genuine tail risk of an abrupt Trump-brokered Q4 announcement, plus the possibility that the price decline partly reflects fading liquidity. Final: ~8.5% Yes.

Will the Bank of Japan announce a 25 bps.rationale: Both forecasters converge near the market anchors (OIS ~81%, Polymarket 84.5%), and the fundamentals — Tokyo core-core at 2.0%, Shunto +5.01%, BOJ's own Outlook flagging inflation 'clearly above' 2% from H2 FY2026, yen still ~159 after a failed $85bn joint intervention, and Reuters' historically reliable BOJ leak channel reporting a September move with government backing — justify sitting at or slightly above those anchors. The critique's strongest points are the correlation of Reuters/OIS/Polymarket signals (one underlying leak, not three independent confirmations) and the fact that a 'different-sized move' would resolve No; however, every BOJ move since 2024 has been exactly 25bps and a 50bps jump is very unlikely, so that tail is worth only ~1-2pts. Offsetting downside risks — EIU's October call, the still-8-1 July hold despite hawkish rhetoric, dovish Takaichi appointee Sato, and a compressed 3-month gap versus historical cadence — keep me from going much above the market. Net: 0.85 Yes, essentially the Polymarket anchor with a modest premium for the sourced leak and a small deduction for the size/timing tails.

Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed.rationale: Forecast 2 is a degenerate 50/50 fallback with zero confidence and no analysis, so it is disregarded. Forecast 1's reasoning holds: late-August transits of ~27-35/day are ~3x the ≤10 PortWatch 7-day-MA threshold, carriers were still phasing back into the Suez corridor, and the 2024-2025 campaign trough never approached 10/day, so a Yes requires a sustained multi-day collapse triggered by a full blockade (e.g., Perim Island seizure) within a ~19-day window. The critique correctly notes the Mocha capture materially raises tail risk and the Aug 7 single-day collapse shows traffic can crater quickly, which argues against discounting far below the Polymarket anchor of 12.7%; however, the rising term structure (21.5% Oct 31, 28% Dec 31) and possible PortWatch reporting lag argue against going above it. I settle at 11% Yes, essentially at the market-implied level with a slight haircut for the short window and measurement mechanics.

Resolution hinges on a narrow data trigger (IMF PortWatch 7-day MA ≤10 arrivals), while proxy transit data sits at 16-37/day and even the worst of the 2024 Houthi campaign bottomed near ~31/day — a 3x cushion above the threshold that has never historically been breached. Reaching ≤10 requires a qualitatively worse-than-2024 event (strait mining, mass vessel losses, insurance-market withdrawal), and carriers are still adding Suez services as of Aug 14, indicating operators do not expect closure. The Polymarket proxy at 8.5% and falling from 33.5% already prices in the July blockade declaration, fatal Aug 12 attack, and premium spikes; the critique is right that undershooting the anchor materially needs justification, so I settle essentially at the market rather than well below it. Offsetting slight upward pressure comes from the compressed ~40-day window with an active Iran-US crisis (expired talks deadline, Aug 17-18 attacks) plus a small allowance for PortWatch data artifacts, which keeps me from dropping to the model's 3-5% low end.

Will Iran target Oman by September 30, 2.rationale: Both forecasters converge near 6-7%, just below the thin Polymarket proxy of 8%, and the critique is right that the anchor is fragile in both directions rather than only overstated. The structural case for No is strong: Oman is Iran's preferred mediator, the Aug 7-8 Hormuz shipping-route agreement was just concluded, Iran characterized its only prior Oman strikes as unintentional, and it is Trump — not Tehran — currently threatening Oman. But the war is unresolved, the 60-day MOU lapsed with no deal, Iran demonstrably hit Duqm/Salalah once during a Gulf-wide retaliation wave, and a second-order path (US coercion over Hormuz via Omani territory triggering Iranian retaliation) is real and unmodeled by either forecaster. Given a ~6-week window with live escalation risk, I hold at the proxy anchor rather than shading below it, landing at 8% YES.

Trump x Greenland deal signed by Decembe.rationale: The direct proxy (Polymarket 14.5%, down from a 66% peak) is the best available anchor and points strongly to No: after 18+ months of talks there is no draft text, no signing date, and Denmark's FM explicitly says several more negotiating rounds are needed, with sovereignty red lines and 85% Greenlandic opposition constraining anything comprehensive. The critique is partly right that both forecasters treated the broad contract definition too lightly — a signed update/addendum to the 1951 Defense Agreement or a security MOU is the analyst-consensus likely outcome and is a much lower bar than acquisition, and Trump has strong incentive for a symbolic signing ceremony before year-end; Kalshi's related 2029 acquisition markets at 21-27% also hint the 14.5% may be a bit low for an 'any agreement' contract. Against that, the close date is Dec 31 2026 with roughly 4-5 months remaining (not 16), so the shorter-horizon hazard framing stands, and the thin-volume Polymarket price argues for wider bands rather than a directional shift. I therefore nudge modestly above both forecasts and above the market anchor to 17% Yes, retaining a dominant No.

Will the Fed decrease interest rates by.rationale: The only same-event market anchor (Polymarket, ~8.15%) sits close to the unconditional historical base rate for an exact -25bp move, consistent with traders classifying 2026 as a pause rather than an easing cycle: five straight holds, a June SEP median dot of 3.8% implying no cuts, rising core PCE (~3.3% projected), and the most hawkish voting pattern in years. Both forecasters correctly identified this, so the consensus direction is sound. However, the critique's strongest point holds: the anchor is thin ($50k, 4.4–12.4% range in three weeks) and there are three unobserved FOMC meetings (Sep/Oct/Nov) before resolution, with a visibly cooling labor market (57K payrolls) and political pressure on Chair Warsh that could tip the reaction function — if a cutting cycle resumes, the conditional base rate for exactly -25bp jumps to ~33%. I therefore push modestly above both forecasts to 12%, adding weight for that regime-shift path while noting the offsetting hike risk keeps the residual firmly in 'No'.

Will Alberta vote for independence in 20.rationale: The Oct 19, 2026 referendum question asked only whether to commence a legal process toward a future binding vote, and pre-vote polling was overwhelming (61-65% Stay vs 30-35%, gap widening), with separation support falling from 28% to 18-19% over the year and Premier Smith actively campaigning and voting 'remain'. The May 2026 Court of King's Bench ruling on First Nations consultation blocks any binding independence vote in the remaining window, and the rival 'Forever Canada' petition nearly doubled the separatist signature count — evidence the critique correctly notes cuts against Yes rather than for it. Residual Yes probability comes from two small tails: an ambiguous resolution reading in which a passed 'process' question counts as a 'framework for independence,' and a surprise polling miss — but both are unlikely given a 30-point gap. I settle at 5%, between the two forecasts and slightly below the exact-question Polymarket anchor of 8%, since the looser Kalshi analog at 17% covers a longer window and is not informative for a 2026-only resolution.

Lee Jae-myung out as president of South.rationale: The identical-question Polymarket market at 9.9% is the cleanest anchor; the Kalshi 53% 'full term' contract covers a 5-year horizon through 2030 and its -30pt slide reflects longer-run legal/political risk rather than a 2026-specific hazard, so it justifies only a modest upward nudge. Structurally, removal via impeachment is near-impossible with the DP holding a blocking majority through 2028 and no motion filed — only a symbolic petition — while Lee's criminal trials are statutorily suspended during his term. The critique's fair points (voluntary resignation under scandal pressure, possible reactivation of suspended trials, and an accelerating approval slide from ~60% to 43-44%) are genuine non-impeachment pathways, but with roughly four months left in the window and no mass protests or coalition fracture reported, they add only a few points of tail risk. I therefore land just modestly below the Polymarket price — reflecting typical long-shot premium on binary 'ouster' markets and the short remaining window — but higher than Forecast 1's 6%, which under-weights the non-impeachment routes flagged by the red team.

The exact-match Polymarket anchor at 10.6% is the best available price, and the structural evidence points below it: impeachment requires 200/300 Assembly votes against a DPK supermajority, no formal motion exists, all five criminal trials remain suspended under Article 84 immunity with no ruling piercing it, and Lee is conducting normal high-profile governance with no health or resignation signals. The critique's points about the Kalshi full-term proxy's 26-point drop and the accelerating approval slide are worth some weight, but the proxy covers a 2030 horizon and approval decline alone (43.3%) is far from the crisis conditions that preceded the Park and Yoon removals; Yoon's own removal required a self-inflicted martial-law declaration. The unresolved constitutional complaint and the ballot-shortage controversy are genuine but low-probability tail paths, and any such escalation would likely take longer than the ~4.5 months remaining in the window. Long-shot 'out' markets also typically carry a small upward bias, so I settle modestly below the direct anchor at 8%.

Russia-Ukraine peace talks by December 3.rationale: The Polymarket anchor at 43.5% (down from 73.5%) is the primary consensus signal and reflects the post-February stall: Putin's rejection of a Zelensky summit, Lavrov's deprioritization of Istanbul, and Russia's mid-August refusal of an immediate ceasefire. I nudge modestly above that anchor because the contract's bar is low (any authorized representatives, mediated formats count), three seemingly qualifying trilateral rounds already occurred in Jan-Feb 2026 (creating genuine latent resolution-ambiguity value the thin $169.5K market may misprice), mediation channels reactivate in bursts rather than at a flat Poisson rate, and ~4.5 months of runway remain with Rubio promising to intensify. Offsetting this: the market's persistent sub-50% level is the best evidence that the resolution source applies a stricter reading (likely direct Russia-Ukraine delegations, excluding US shuttle/track-two), no formal round is scheduled, and the TASS Witkoff/Kushner 'may visit' report is unconfirmed state-media framing deserving heavy discount. The critique's point about excessive narrowness is noted, but for a binary the tail scenarios (escalation forcing snap talks vs. total breakdown) largely offset, so I hold close to a near-coinflip slightly favoring No.

Will the Republicans win the Wisconsin g.rationale: The best available market anchor (Polymarket 23.5% YES) converges with an independent base-rate/polling blend model at 23–26%, and both post-primary polls (Crowley +3 to +4) and the national environment (generic ballot D+5–8, Trump net approval ~-20) point toward a Democratic hold, as does the ~77% out-party success rate in open-seat midterm swing-state governor races and Wisconsin's 2025 D+10 Supreme Court result. Counterweights are real: Wisconsin's near-even partisan baseline (2024 R+0.9), Tiffany's large cash advantage and 7-figure ad blitz, and Crowley's narrow 39.8% upset primary win with low statewide name ID — all of which justify a Republican probability meaningfully above the 15% level. The critique is right that the Polymarket anchor is thin and that ~11 weeks of unmodeled campaign dynamics remain, which argues for slightly more probability on the trailing side rather than tighter concentration; that pushes me marginally above the raw market price. Resolution-timing quibbles don't change the binary allocation since eventual certification resolves it either way. Final: 26% Yes / 74% No, essentially the consensus with a small upward tilt for staleness and money asymmetry.

The Polymarket anchor (22.5% YES) plus the historical base rate (president's party lost WI governorship in 7 of 9 cycles since 1990) and the D+7/+8 national environment all point strongly toward a Democratic hold, and both forecasters correctly landed near that anchor. However, the critique makes two fair points: the anchor rests on a thin ($92K) market whose -37% one-week move likely overshot, and the only general-election polls are from early August showing a 3-point lead well inside MOE with three months of campaign left in the nation's most evenly divided state. Tiffany's large resource edge and Crowley's sub-40% chaotic primary win (a potential unity/quality risk) are genuine tail supports for a Republican upset that neither forecaster fully priced. I therefore nudge modestly above both the market and the consensus forecasts to 26% for Yes, while keeping the clear directional lean toward a Crowley/Democratic win.

Will Delcy Rodríguez be the de facto lea.rationale: Rodríguez has exercised de facto executive and military authority for ~8 months (sworn in Jan 5, 2026; public military allegiance in February; cabinet reshuffle in March; removal of Padrino López in July), and the US treats her as its governing partner while explicitly declining to push a Machado/González transition or elections — all of which point strongly to Yes. The best available same-event market anchor (Polymarket, 90%, stable) is consistent with this, though its thin $89k volume warrants modest discounting rather than full deference. The critique's strongest points are that multiple partially independent failure modes exist over the ~4.5 months past the research cutoff — a Cabello move (potentially telegraphed by his ally now heading the defense ministry), a US policy reversal, a health/vacuum event, or genuine ambiguity about co-authority with Jorge Rodríguez/Cabello — which collectively justify shading below the market anchor rather than above it. The generic 43-67% interim-leader survival model deserves little weight because it conditions on day-one incumbency, whereas she has already survived the highest-hazard period. Net: 88% Yes.

Will CDU/CSU–SPD German federal coalitio.rationale: The Polymarket price of 15% is the only live anchor and it already prices the remaining ~4.5-month window, so Forecast 1's downward adjustment for a shrinking horizon double-counts information the market has: the correct starting point is ~15%, not a re-derived base rate. Structural factors strongly favor survival — CDU/CSU hold only 208/630 seats with no alternative partner, both governing parties poll at historic lows against a surging AfD (making a snap election mutually suicidal), Merz has publicly committed to the full term, and the July 2, 2026 reform package demonstrates functional cooperation. The critique correctly notes residual upside risk the forecasters underweighted: SPD-side withdrawal (Bas's collapse warning) is not controlled by Merz's commitments, and the Sept 6/Sept 20 eastern state elections are discrete repricing events that could spike the hazard for the final three months. Against that, the resolution bar is strict (formal withdrawal, mass ministerial resignation, or new government) — leadership churn atop either party would not qualify — and no prior CDU/CSU–SPD grand coalition has broken early. Netting a slight longshot-bias discount on dramatic-event contracts against genuine near-term trigger risk, I settle marginally below the anchor at 13%.

Unit FDV above $200M one day after launc.rationale: Both forecasts converged on 0.34 by back-solving to the Polymarket proxy anchor (36.5%), and the critique is right that they under-weighted the ~2-year runway and the $350K ticker purchase, which push launch odds somewhat higher than the ~50-60% assumed; conversely, the revenue-to-HYPE-buyback structure and low-FDV secondary-infra precedent are genuine independent bearish factors for the conditional FDV leg. Decomposing: ~60% chance a UNIT token launches by Dec 31, 2027, and conditional on a launch of a $1B+ TVL, 'S-tier' bridge with strong ecosystem attention, roughly 60-65% chance day-one FDV clears $200M (the precedent set is bimodal — HYPE-style debut clears easily, minor-infra debut does not), yielding ~0.36-0.40. The Polymarket decline from 67% to 36.5% is informative but on only $103K volume, so it deserves modest rather than heavy weight, and it may partly reflect near-term timing decay rather than a full-horizon view. I therefore sit essentially at the anchor rather than below it, nudging marginally above both forecasts to 0.36 Yes / 0.64 No.

Will Anthropic be the #3 AI Lab at the e.rationale: The best available anchor is the thin Polymarket sibling at 7.5% YES, which repriced sharply down from 37% as Anthropic's July–Aug 2026 releases (Opus 5, Fable 5 rebaseline) pushed its models to the top of model-level boards. 'Exactly #3' is a narrow target requiring precisely two labs (most plausibly Google and OpenAI) to sit above Anthropic — a two-sided containment condition that neither generic volatility nor the #1-frequency base rate directly supports. The critique is right that the analysis rests on unverified aggregator data with no live official Lab Rank pull, and that the ~20% Markov base rate deserves some weight, so I widen above the market print rather than converging at 7-10%. However, the resolution horizon from the latest evidence (Aug 2026) is short, limiting the scope for a two-lab overtake, which caps the upward adjustment. I settle at 12% YES — modestly above the thin market anchor, well below the flat-prior base-rate model.

Will AfD win an absolute majority of sea.rationale: Consensus seat projections (INSA, pollytix, Wikipedia, Aug 2026) place AfD at 39 of 83 seats on 41-42% vote share, three short of the 42-seat majority. Working the threshold mechanics explicitly: AfD needs roughly >16% of votes wasted on sub-5% parties (FDP ~4, Grüne ~4, others ~4 already gets ~12%), so the Yes path essentially hinges on BSW (~5%) also missing while AfD holds 42%+ — a plausible but conjunctive and knife-edge scenario, and SPD at ~6% is not a credible additional failure candidate. Historical precedent (no Sachsen-Anhalt majority ever; AfD underperforming 2021 pre-election expectations), high-salience tactical consolidation behind CDU/Linke, and the small tail risk embedded in the 'No' definition (election not occurring/confirmed by Jan 31, 2027) all shade below the 31.5% Polymarket proxy. I land modestly under both forecasts and the market at 27%, acknowledging the mechanism is genuinely live rather than remote.

The core arithmetic is closer than both forecasters allowed: with AfD at 41–43% and CDU ~24%, Linke ~12.5%, SPD ~8%, the residual pool (BSW ~4%, Grüne ~4%, FDP, Freie Wähler, others) is roughly 13–15%, so if most of it fails the 5% hurdle AfD needs only ~43–44% for 49/97 seats — i.e., current polling is at the knife edge rather than clearly short. That makes the ~13% 'central' seat-math figure look too pessimistic, and the critique's point 6 is well taken; the true distribution is closer to the live Polymarket read (29.5%) than to a 20% blend. Offsetting factors keep me just below the market: Grüne clearing 5% would push the bar to ~46%, tactical anti-AfD consolidation and late CDU firming are real, no AfD state majority has ever occurred, and the Polymarket price has been trending down (53.5% → 29.5%), suggesting recent information favors No. I therefore land at 26% Yes, above both submitted forecasts but modestly below the market anchor.

Will Hibachi launch a token by December.rationale: The only live anchor is Polymarket at 35.5% YES, which most plausibly corresponds to the same Dec 31, 2026 horizon and already prices in the confirmed $HEAT ticker, the Circle/Arc backing, and the ~9 months of remaining runway. Structural negatives are real: no announced TGE date, TGE explicitly gated on the Arc FX rollout, an already-resolved-No March 2026 sub-deadline, and 17+ months elapsed since the points program began (past the Hyperliquid ~13-month benchmark). The devil's advocate correctly notes offsetting upside (partial Arc FX markets reportedly live, fast comparables like Aster, institutional Circle involvement) and offsetting downside (the 71.5% peak looks like Feb-2026 announcement euphoria, so 35.5% may still be optimistic) — these roughly cancel, justifying staying at the market rather than deviating. I therefore hold essentially at the anchor with no meaningful edge claim.

Will Donald Trump visit Ukraine by Decem.rationale: The identical Polymarket contract at ~7.1% is the best anchor, and the fundamentals corroborate No: Trump has explicitly conditioned a personal Ukraine visit on the war ending, peace talks stalled repeatedly through 2026, it is Witkoff/Kushner rather than Trump who are traveling to Kyiv, and no advance logistics or itinerary exist. However, the critique fairly notes the anchor is thin ($97k volume) and extremely volatile (50%→7% in 30 days), and the historical/hazard-based model implies materially higher odds (~21-23% absent a ceasefire), so a point estimate hugging the market understates tail paths: a ceasefire-linked 'victory lap' visit, a symbolic post-envoy trip, or a midterm-season surprise within the ~4.5-month window. I therefore set YES modestly above the market at 10%, blending the market anchor with partial weight on the base-rate model while keeping No heavily favored given the absence of any concrete scheduling signal.

Surf FDV above $50M one day after launch.rationale: This is a compound event: a Surf TGE must occur by Dec 31, 2027 AND day-1 FDV must exceed $50M. The critique's strongest point is that both forecasters implicitly assumed P(launch) ~50% despite a window extending well beyond the research snapshot — a live product, fresh $15M Pantera/Coinbase/DCG funding, and an active pre-TGE farming community imply cumulative launch odds nearer 55-65%. That upward adjustment is largely offset by the critique's other valid point: the conditional clear-rate is likely below 85%, since Recall (the closest comp) launched at just ~$58M and the 2025 high-FDV/low-float backlash pushes teams toward deliberately conservative, higher-float launch valuations, plus a weak crypto/AI-agent backdrop (ElizaOS wind-down). Multiplying ~0.60 x ~0.75 lands right back near the 42% Polymarket anchor, so despite thin liquidity ($90k notional) and the sharp 86%→42% slide, I hold essentially at the anchor rather than drifting below both forecasts.

US ceasefire against Iran continues thro.rationale: The only anchor is a thin Polymarket quote at 56.5% Yes with no Kalshi-direct price, so it deserves only partial weight. Independent hazard math argues for shading lower: three confirmed qualifying US strike events in 2026 (Feb, May, mid-July) imply roughly one incident per ~2 months during active tension, and the ~6-week window after the Aug 17 MOU expiry arrives with an expired agreement, reimposed naval blockade, and an explicit, already-prepared Pickaxe Mountain tripwire — corroborated by the cross-market cluster (blockade-ends 34.5%, nuclear-deal 11.5%) that prices continued instability. Offsetting this, the resolution bar is strict: only a confirmed direct US air/missile strike on Iranian soil counts, so Israeli-only strikes, blockade enforcement, naval incidents, and further threat cycles all resolve Yes, and Trump has demonstrably stood down prepared strikes (Aug 1-2) in exchange for negotiation time. Balancing the elevated but escapable hazard against the narrow definition, I land marginally below the market at 52% Yes, close to but slightly under both forecasters' consensus.

Will Bernie endorse James Talarico for T.rationale: The tagged market price of 57.5% is the primary anchor, but its steep decline (90.5% peak, -15% in 30d, -12.5% in 7d) after the primary uncertainty was already resolved is meaningful information rather than noise — it plausibly reflects traders internalizing that Sanders substitutes visible campaigning (June TX convention headline) for formal endorsement language. Bullish considerations remain real: Talarico is the confirmed nominee with strong anti-oligarchy alignment, the race is highly competitive (Paxton at ~52%), Sanders is actively issuing endorsements this cycle, and three months of general-election runway gives many natural occasions for explicit language. Bearish considerations are the 'too early' January comment, Heinrich (not Sanders) endorsing first, the 'Bernie blowback' selectivity narrative, and genuine resolution-criteria risk if Sanders never uses explicit endorsement wording. I therefore shade modestly below the anchor and below both forecasters, landing at 54% Yes with wide effective uncertainty.

Felix Protocol FDV above $25M one day af.rationale: The ticker-matched Polymarket direct price of 8.5% is the primary anchor, and it has repriced sharply downward (72% high → 18.5% a month ago → 8.5%), consistent with fading expectations that Felix holds a TGE at all before the Dec 31, 2026 deadline. The critique's decomposition point is the strongest challenge: for a protocol with $167M–$1B+ TVL, multi-product breadth and $800K+ revenue, P(FDV>$25M | launch) is plausibly 70-85% (HyperLend is a smaller, weaker comp; Kinetiq is the more apt one), which implies the market is effectively pricing P(launch by end-2026) at only ~10-12% rather than the stale ~50% news figure. I resolve that tension in favor of the direct feed but not fully — the thin $94.5K volume, wide 7%-72% history, unresolved 60% news citation, and Hyperliquid-ecosystem resilience (HYPE +7.8%) all justify a modest premium above the anchor. Net: ~12% Yes, with the dominant failure mode simply being no token launch within the window rather than a sub-$25M valuation.

Will Ukraine re-enter Obratne or Temyriv.rationale: Both villages fell in Aug 2025 and the front subsequently moved well past them; no source reports ISW shading Ukrainian re-entry at either named village, only localized gains at adjacent settlements in Mar-Apr 2026, and ISW characterized the Huliaipole sector as concluded and de-prioritized by Aug 2026. With only weeks remaining and a persistence requirement that would filter out brief raids, the hazard of a qualifying, sustained re-entry is low. The critique's point about the code_execution 16-17% estimate is not persuasive since that is a derived hazard model with an arbitrary activity assumption, not evidence of activity at these specific villages; the ceasefire tail is real but no negotiated territorial terms cover this area. I hold the consensus at 7% YES, consistent with the Polymarket anchor of 8% and the static-sector evidence.

Both forecasters converge on a strong No, and the underlying base rate supports that: Obratne and Temyrivka fell during 2025 Russian advances on the Hulyaipole axis where Russian forces have held the initiative, and Ukrainian recaptures of named settlements in Zaporizhzhia have been rare and typically confined to the immediate contact line. The critique's strongest points — the long horizon to Sept 2026, the 'either village' OR structure, the relatively low ISW bar (a shaded gain/counteroffensive layer persisting one update cycle, which ISW sometimes applies to claimed local Ukrainian counterattacks), and genuine uncertainty about exact frontline distance — justify nudging Yes modestly above the 7-9% consensus. Conversely, the ceasefire pathway adds little: any negotiated freeze would most plausibly lock in current lines rather than transfer these specific villages back to Ukrainian actual control. With no Kalshi anchor available, I settle slightly above both forecasters at ~11% Yes to reflect the data gaps and tail-scenario breadth without abandoning the dominant directional evidence.

Will Russia capture Serhiivka by Decembe.rationale: The best available consensus anchor (Polymarket 17%, falling from a 41.5% high on bearish news flow) and the ground reporting agree: as of mid-Aug 2026 Serhiivka is still described only as an objective Russia is attacking 'toward,' with no ISW confirmation of capture and no significant net Russian advance west of Pokrovsk since Dec 2025. The critique is right that the brief's stochastic distance/rate model implies far higher capture odds, but that model's inputs (0.5-2 km/mo effective advance) are contradicted by the observed near-zero net rate in this exact sector, where the 2025 Dobropillia offensive was fully reversed; the market price is better information than the model's optimistic grid. I do allow a real Yes tail for the Pokrovsk-style scenario where a long grind suddenly resolves, plus the possibility that ISW shading lags pro-Russian claims of gains near Novopodhorodne by weeks — that keeps me from moving below the market despite Ukraine's counteroffensive successes elsewhere. Thin liquidity ($33.7k) argues for only modest deference, so I land essentially at the anchor: ~16% Yes.

Russia x Ukraine Peace Parlay.rationale: The parlay requires three concurrent conditions by 2026-12-31, and the binding constraint is clearly the signed peace deal leg: Ukrainian HUR (Aug 18, 2026) explicitly assesses Russia will not sign by year-end and intends to take all of Donetsk, while Russia rejected even a partial Black Sea truce on Aug 14. Even granting the critique's point that a ceasefire alone may be plausible in 2026 (Chinese academic view), a formally signed comprehensive treaty within ~4.5 months, plus a codified NATO renunciation, remains the choke point — and any narrower ceasefire-only or framework outcome resolves NO, which asymmetrically favors No rather than widening YES. The Polymarket anchor of 8.5% is thin ($600K volume) but its steady decline (18.5%→8.5%) is directionally consistent with the ~7.7% historical base rate for signed treaties within 12 months of talks and with conjunctive model estimates of 7-13%. I shade modestly below the anchor to 6% for the compressed window and uniformly negative freshest evidence, while leaving enough mass for a surprise Trump-brokered breakthrough given active US engagement in July-August 2026.

Will Russia enter Krasnopillya by Septem.rationale: The Sumy axis has been repeatedly assessed as stalled by ISW/CTP from June through mid-August 2026, with Russia relying on 1-3 man infiltration groups and nationwide gains concentrated in Donetsk/Zaporizhzhia. Krasnopillya has only been hit by standoff strikes, and the nearest ISW-shaded Russian positions are roughly 30 km away, requiring ~0.7 km/day sustained advance against active Ukrainian counterattacks — far above realistic tempo, giving a model estimate of 1-5%. However, the critique is right that two genuine upside pathways remain underweighted: the unresolved '9 km from frontline' framing (if any forward ground contact is nearer than the geodesic estimate) and resolution ambiguity where a small infiltration group reaching the settlement's edge could trigger ISW contested/claimed shading. That, plus a six-week data gap and the possibility Gerasimov's buffer-zone directive produces a late-season push, keeps me modestly above the pure model range but still well below the thinly traded 10.9% Polymarket proxy, which has been trending down from a 49% peak.

Will Ukraine re-enter Huliaipole by Octo.rationale: Russia has held Huliaipole since ISW's Feb 6, 2026 confirmation, and control was reconfirmed after the brief late-June contested period; by mid-August the front was stabilized just outside town with Ukraine defending rather than assaulting, and DeepState's Pohorilyi saw no recapture signs. The negotiated path does not help Yes either, since draft terms would freeze rather than reverse Zaporizhzhia lines and Lavrov rejected even a freeze. The resolution bar is strict (ISW-shaded Ukrainian control persisting a full update cycle — the June contest reportedly did not clear it), which argues for pushing below the thin, low-volume Polymarket 21% anchor toward the brief's 2–9% model range. I nudge slightly above the model's ~4% center to account for the ~2.5-month data gap and the demonstrated pattern of periodic Ukrainian contestation at the town's edges, landing at 9%.

Yoon out of custody before 2027?.rationale: Yoon is no longer a pretrial detainee whose warrant can lapse: he holds a Supreme Court–finalized 7-year obstruction sentence plus a first-instance life sentence under appeal, so even a favorable insurrection ruling would leave a binding term to serve, making a technical release or bail hearing pathway largely moot. With roughly four months left in the window and no pardon signal from the opposition-aligned Lee government, the structural routes to release (pardon, full acquittal, health furlough, political upheaval amnesty) are each individually improbable and collectively worth only a few points. The critique's tail pathways (medical release, remand-triggered release, snap political amnesty) justify not going below ~4%, but they are offset by the same critique's point that the market may still be slightly stale relative to the finalized sentence. I therefore settle marginally below the 7.55% Polymarket anchor at 5% Yes, consistent with both forecasters and the declining price trend.

Will Ukraine re-enter Obratne or Temyriv.rationale: The hard evidence chain runs toward No: both villages fell in summer 2025, Russia took Huliaipole itself in Jan 2026, the latest available reporting (Aug 2026) describes the sector as static with no confirmed Ukrainian re-entry, Ukraine's big 2026 gains came on the separate Oleksandrivka axis, and any negotiated freeze would leave these villages Russian-held. That structural picture supports something near the Fermi model's 8-20% band. However, the resolution bar is genuinely low (ISW shading in either of two villages, including transient advance/contested shading that persists one cycle), these villages were explicitly named Ukrainian counteroffensive objectives in Dec 2025, the sector has demonstrated month-to-month reversibility, and the only market anchor (Polymarket 57.5%, +21% in 30d) plus a 4-month data blackout suggest possible developments not captured in the brief. Balancing a discounted-but-not-dismissed market signal against a strong structural case for No, I land modestly below both forecasters' midpoint-to-high end at 0.33, with wide acknowledged uncertainty from the thin liquidity and missing recent map data.

Lee Jae-myung arrested before 2027?.rationale: Article 84 immunity actively shields Lee: all five criminal cases are suspended, two courts have upheld immunity's extension to pre-presidency proceedings, no warrant or new prosecutorial step targets him, and his party's Assembly majority blocks the 200-vote impeachment threshold that would be a prerequisite for any Yoon-style detention. Fundamentals arguably imply 2-3%, but the red team is right that the Yoon precedent shows South Korean crises can escalate from 'structurally impossible' to removal-and-detention within months, and there is genuine opacity around insurrection/treason-exception or Constitutional Court reversal pathways — plus the sharp Kalshi 'full term' decline (93%→53%) signals real tenure instability that could partially overlap arrest-adjacent scenarios. I therefore do not shade far below the direct Polymarket anchor (8.35%, slightly declining, decent $530k volume), settling just under it at 6% to reflect both the strong structural No case and the short remaining window (only months to end-2026) balanced against irreducible political tail risk. This lands between the two forecasts while explicitly crediting the critique's tail-risk concerns rather than compressing toward the low end.

Theo FDV above $100M one day after launc.rationale: The binding constraint is launch timing, not valuation: no TGE date, token contract, or airdrop date exists, and the market auto-resolves No absent a launch by Dec 31, 2026 — with the brief's timeline already running into March 2026, the runway is short. Conditional on a launch, FDV >$100M is highly likely (~85%) given $20M+ token-warrant funding from Hack VC/Anthos, a $100M Genesis Vault, and EigenLayer/Symbiotic precedents under low-float/high-FDV tokenomics, which implies the market is effectively pricing P(launch) at roughly 27%. That decomposition argues for a modest premium over the 22.5% Polymarket proxy, but offsetting factors — thin ~$81K volume that could equally be noise in either direction, a bearish macro backdrop (BTC -17%, ETH -11%), end-of-window resolution mechanics for a late-December launch, and the possibility of a deliberately constrained initial float — cap that premium. I settle just below the two forecasters' 24% at 23%, respecting the anchor and its sharply negative trend while acknowledging the strong conditional base rate.

Will the Republicans win the Georgia Sen.rationale: Every public poll since the June runoff shows Ossoff ahead of Collins (average ~+6.7, with even the GOP-aligned Fabrizio poll at Ossoff +9), the generic ballot sits at D+6 to D+8, Ossoff holds a large fundraising edge, and Cook shifted Georgia toward Democrats — all consistent with the Polymarket proxy of ~7% for a GOP win and its downward trend. I hold modestly above that market proxy because Georgia is a genuine swing state (Trump +2.2 in 2024; Ossoff won by 1.2 in 2021), the polling is roughly three months stale relative to Election Day, and the majority/runoff rule plus the possibility that public polls understate a Trump-endorsed nominee create real tail risk. The critique's runoff point cuts both ways — Democrats actually won the 2021 and 2022 Georgia runoffs — so it justifies uncertainty rather than a clear upward shift, and the 'toss-up' analyst ratings are largely lagging labels for a race with a consistent mid-single-digit lead. Balancing the possibility of further Democratic consolidation (which would argue sub-7%) against late tightening, ~10% for a Republican win is the calibrated landing spot.

Will the Democratic Party win the VA-06.rationale: VA-06 is roughly R+17 PVI, voted Trump+24, and Cline has won by 28-40 points in every race; he is running again with no serious primary opposition, and the Virginia Supreme Court's reversal of the mid-decade redistricting amendment removed the only realistic structural path to a Democratic flip. Districts at PVI >R+15 with an incumbent essentially never flip absent an open seat or scandal, and swing modeling puts organic flip probability at ~1-4% even in a D+5-8 environment. I discount the thin $68K Polymarket price of 8.5% partially for favorite-longshot bias, but the critique is right that I should not push all the way to the model floor: unmeasured 2025 Virginia Democratic overperformance, residual legal/redistricting tail risk, and late scandal/retirement scenarios justify keeping a modest cushion above the ~2% fundamentals estimate. Final call of 5% sits between both forecasters and below the market anchor, reflecting a clear but not certain 'No'.

Will there be between 11 and 13 earthqua.rationale: With ~10–11 M7.0+ events already logged by mid-August (62% of the year elapsed) and a baseline expectation of ~5–6 further events in the remaining 4.5 months, the year needs an unusually quiet finish to land in [11,13]: a Poisson calculation gives ~9% if the current tally is 11 and ~20% if it is 10, blending to roughly 12–14%. The Polymarket proxy anchor (9.5%, falling, with 14–16 at 42% and 17–19 at 36%) is consistent with this pace-based view. I sit modestly above the market anchor to respect the critique's points: the tally is uncertain (10 vs 11), magnitude revisions cut both ways, clustering in the observed timeline suggests over-dispersion (which fattens the low-count tail as well as the high), and the sub-11 tail is not strictly zero. Unconditional base rates (23–29%) are largely superseded now that most of the year is observed above trend, so the final call stays clearly on No while widening slightly toward Yes versus the raw market price.

The 11–13 band is a narrow 3-count window against a long-run rate of ~14–15/yr, so 'No' is mechanically favored (it spans both ≤10 and ≥14); empirical base rates give 20–31% and Poisson/gamma-Poisson baselines 25–30%. The critique's key point has merit: 5 confirmed M7.0+ through April is roughly a 15/yr pace, not a genuine slowdown, and unconfirmed June–July Japan/Philippines events could push YTD to ~7 — a Bayesian update on this evidence yields a posterior annual rate near 13–15 and P(11–13) ≈ 27–35%, above both forecasters' 23–24%. Offsetting this, the Polymarket proxy at 18.5% (down from 36%) reflects fresher YTD information than the brief and plausibly signals the count drifting out of the band on one side, and threshold/revision ambiguity adds noise that hurts a tight bucket more than the wide complement. Blending the proxy market anchor with the somewhat more favorable structural model, I settle modestly above both prior forecasts at 26% Yes.

Will the ECB announce a 25 bps increase.rationale: The direct Polymarket contract at 87.5% YES and rising is the best anchor, corroborated by near-full OIS pricing, a Reuters analyst consensus for a September 25bp hike, above-target HICP (2.8%) amid an energy shock, and Lagarde explicitly leaving the door open. The stale base-rate model (~8%) is miscalibrated for an active tightening cycle and is rightly discounted by both forecasters. The critique's valid points — a ~3-week data blackout before an explicitly data-dependent decision, the possibility of a non-25bp move (e.g., 50bp) resolving No, and the contract's wide 15%-89.5% 62-day range showing high news sensitivity — justify sitting at or slightly below the market rather than above it. I therefore settle at 0.865 for Yes, essentially at the anchor with a modest haircut for late data and size-tail risk.

Both forecasters converge near 0.78-0.79 by blending Polymarket's 83% with news-cited OIS trackers at 70-78%, and the fundamental case is genuinely strong: the ECB already restarted hiking in June, held in July only with hawks pushing for immediate action, Lagarde explicitly kept September 'live,' and July HICP rose to 2.9%/2.5% with energy +10% y/y. However the critique lands on two legitimate discounts: the Polymarket anchor is thin ($69k, 15%-89.5% range in 54 days) and already cooling (-3.5% in 7 days), and the contract requires exactly 25bp, so a small tail of a 50bp move or no-move-after-oil-retreat also resolves No. The decision is also unusually contingent on September staff projections and oil path that are simply unknown as of the brief, which argues for slightly wider bands than the tight ~0.79 consensus. I therefore settle just below both forecasts and below the Polymarket print, near the top of the OIS-implied range.

Will FaZe win a Tier 1 event in 2026?.rationale: The only market anchor (Polymarket, 13.85% YES and trending down) aligns with the qualitative record: no S-Tier title in 2025-2026, karrigan's confirmed departure leaving a post-IGL rebuild, the first missed Major in org history, and repeated 12th-15th placings alongside only mid-tier podiums. The devil's advocate correctly notes the quant model's wider range and possible additional S-Tier events beyond PGL Singapore, which argues against shading much below the market — so I settle essentially at the anchor rather than the 11% floor, since cumulative opportunity across several remaining S-Tier LANs plus a Major partly offsets qualification risk. Conversely, the model's ~40% central estimate was explicitly calibrated to a stale 25-35% price band and assumes a per-event win rate FaZe's 2026 results simply don't support, so it deserves little weight. Net: 12% YES, a hair below a thin, declining market price, reflecting deteriorating fundamentals balanced against residual pedigree and multi-event upside.

U.S. forces in Gaza before 2027?.rationale: The Polymarket same-market anchor sits at 7% and trends down, but that price covered a longer window; with data through August 2026 and only ~4 months remaining, time decay justifies a modest discount. Every substantive channel points No: US personnel remain at the CMCC in Kiryat Gat (now winding down), the ISF is by design non-US on the ground with only a symbolic ~200-troop Rafah pilot approved, and the US support base is being built on the Gaza border rather than inside. The critique rightly flags two live tails — a contested resolution if Gen. Jeffers or liaison staff cross into Gaza (though command/advisory roles appear carved out) and a ceasefire collapse pulling in guarantor forces — but the Sinai MFO/UNIFIL precedent argues US ground presence is structurally avoided even during flare-ups, pushing the base rate lower. Balancing the ambiguity tail upward against the strong structural prior downward, I land at 5% Yes, slightly below the market anchor.

Will DeepSeek be added to the Chinese Mi.rationale: The best available anchor (Polymarket ~27%, thin but directionally informative after decaying from a 55.5% peak) sits near the structural base-rate central estimate of 25-35%, and both forecasters landed inside that band. The strongest case-specific evidence is asymmetric toward No: DeepSeek was singled out for exclusion from the June 2026 1260H update despite explicit bipartisan letters naming it, and the administration also held its Commerce Entity List designation despite interagency approval — indicating a durable, DeepSeek-specific political carve-out rather than a mere processing lag, reinforced by litigation-driven caution around contested designations. Offsetting this, roughly one more annual-ish DoD update window remains before June 30, 2027, congressional pressure is recurring with a demonstrated 8-12 month lag effect, and a legislative mandate (FY2027 NDAA / Blocking CCP Spy Tech Act) or a sudden shift in US-China tension calculus could force action — a real but minority pathway over a 12-month horizon. Netting the downward pull of the carve-out signal against the upward pull of legislative/trigger pathways leaves me essentially at the anchor, ~25% Yes.

Will there be Saudi Arabian military act.rationale: The evidence brief documents multiple independently reported Saudi strikes on Yemeni territory within the window (Mukalla port and Hadramout in Dec 2025 per CNN/PBS; Sana'a airport and Hodeidah in July 2026 per multiple outlets), plus reciprocal Houthi attacks on Saudi soil — a pattern that, taken at face value, already satisfies the YES condition, and the question text does not restrict qualifying action to anti-Houthi operations. Forecast 1's heavy reliance on a ~$15k, sharply declining Polymarket proxy is internally inconsistent with the brief's own characterization of that market as thin and unexplained, so I discount it substantially rather than treat it as an efficient anchor. However, I do not go as high as Forecast 2's 90%: the price decline is anomalous enough that it may encode a real resolution-criteria problem (Riyadh has apparently never officially confirmed any strike; several reports are rebel-media sourced), and the underlying news synthesis carries some sourcing risk. Netting the strong direct evidence against genuine resolution/attribution risk and market divergence, I settle near 0.79 for Yes.

Will Ethereum reach $2,000 in August?.rationale: Resolution needs only a single 1-minute Binance wick ≥$2,000, but spot ~$1,878–$1,910 sits ~5–6% below the barrier with ~15 days left and no August print above $1,935. A first-passage calculation using the actually observed compressed vol regime (7-day band of only ~4.3%, implying ~30–40% annualized) gives ~40–53% touch probability, materially below the ~60–80% figure derived from generic crypto vol assumptions; the critique is right that the recent regime is the more relevant evidence and that both forecasters split the difference too generously toward Yes. Corroborating bearish signals — repeated rejection at the 100-day EMA (~$1,924), analyst point ranges capped at $1,928–$1,950, and a flat-to-slightly-declining Polymarket trend — argue the true probability sits at or just below the 54.5% Polymarket proxy, which is thin ($238.6k volume, 17 data points, no sibling ladder) and thus deserves partial rather than dominant weight. I retain meaningful Yes mass for a dovish-Fed/CPI or short-squeeze spike (only ~5% needed intraday), landing modestly below both prior forecasts at 47% Yes.

Will the U.S. lift CAATSA sanctions on T.rationale: As of the latest reporting (~mid-August 2026), no qualifying formal action exists: State explicitly reaffirmed CAATSA §231/NDAA §1245 policy is 'unchanged,' the F-35/CAATSA package is reported 'stalled,' the S-400 precondition is unresolved, and any executive move triggers congressional review amid bipartisan resistance. The thin Polymarket print (32.5%, $15k volume, decaying -12.5 pts in 30 days) deserves heavy discount as it may reflect a few traders rather than crowd wisdom, and hazard modeling over the remaining ~75 days implies only ~5-17%. I nudge slightly above the model mid-case (~10%) to account for the Trump wildcard — a unilateral, symbolically framed waiver/delisting timed as a pre-midterm diplomatic win is plausible and would resolve Yes even without Hill buy-in — plus the possibility that a smooth F110 engine clearance signals loosening resistance. Netting these, ~15% for Yes sits between the base-rate model's upper bound and the discounted market anchor, closer to Forecast 1 than Forecast 2.

Will Russia capture Verkhnia Tersa by Se.rationale: The direct Polymarket anchor (9.5-10% YES) plus mid-August Ukrainian General Staff reporting that Russia is still only 'attempting' advances toward Verkhnia Tersa both point strongly to No, and no ceasefire pathway exists that would transfer control diplomatically. The devil's advocate makes two fair points that justify a modest upward nudge above both forecasters' 11%: the evidence is stale (mid-August) with ~6 weeks of unobserved fighting during a period of slight Russian reacceleration (33 sq mi/4 weeks), and the anchor is a thin market (~$48-51K, 18 data points) whose swing from 49% to 10% signals genuine volatility rather than confident pricing. Reference-class precedent (Avdiivka, Bakhmut) also shows fortified villages can collapse nonlinearly after long 'stabilized' phases, and fighting is already in/around the village. Still, the dominant evidence — heavy fortification since 2022, front described as halted, Ukrainian counter-gains nearby, and the prior May 31 market resolving No despite similar imminence narratives — keeps this firmly in No territory at ~13% Yes.

Will Russia capture Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi by.rationale: Both forecasters landed at 10-11% by essentially hugging a thinly-traded ($47k) Polymarket price, and the critique correctly notes that anchor is volatile (42% to 9% in a month) and low-information, while the brief's own military indicators (ISW's Aug 13 framing of the Pishchane–Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi split as an active in-progress objective, DeepState's confirmed ~3 sq km gain, repeated local claims) argue for something above the bottom of the 6-50% Monte Carlo range. Offsetting that, the resolution bar is structurally biased toward No: it requires persistent ISW red shading through a subsequent update cycle, and ISW/DeepState have classified nine-plus months of Russian presence there as infiltration rather than control despite repeated Gerasimov claims — so even de facto Russian presence may not resolve Yes within six weeks. Army-wide tempo (~1.22 sq km/day) is very slow and one analyst assessment suggests the axis may be deprioritized, with no ceasefire path that would transfer the settlement. I therefore move modestly above both forecasts and the market to 13%, crediting the critique's momentum and liquidity points while keeping No strongly favored given the demonstrated confirmation lag and stalled offensive.

US announces withdrawal from Al Udeid Ai.rationale: No US official statement of withdrawal exists, and the strongest policy signals (EO 14353 security guarantee, Dec 2025 Strategic Dialogue reaffirming Al Udeid infrastructure upgrades, Aug 2026 CENTCOM drone-force standup) point toward continued presence; the January 2026 evacuation was reversed within days and the July 2026 'emptied base' claims trace to Iranian state media. However, the red team is right that both forecasters drifted too far below the most direct anchor: Polymarket at 7% with real money and rising trend is pricing live war information (an unresolved Iran-Israel-US conflict as of Aug 2026) plus resolution-criteria ambiguity about what counts as a 'qualifying announcement,' neither of which the ~0.2% structural base rate captures. I therefore stay close to the market rather than the base rate, shading only slightly down for the short remaining window (~6 weeks) and the fact that no evacuation to date has been framed as policy-level. Final: 6% Yes.

Edi Rama out as Albania PM in 2026?.rationale: Rama's structural position is strong: a fresh May 2025 mandate with 83/140 seats, demonstrated bloc discipline (82-47 vote shielding Balluku), no active no-confidence mechanism, no personal indictment, and repeated explicit refusals to resign — plus a 12-year record of surviving major scandals. The Polymarket analogue at 19.5% is the only market anchor but is thin ($131K) and has swung 13.5-53%, suggesting news-driven overpricing; the Albania-specific Fermi base rate of ~9-11% is arguably more informative, so I shade below the market. The critique's fair points — an 'any interruption' clause that broadens qualifying events, ~5 months of unobserved developments with an escalating protest trend, a specific SPAK-reaches-Rama pathway (Ahmetaj's allegation that Rama 'directed all key decisions'), and EU conditionality pressure — justify keeping a meaningful tail rather than collapsing to the pure base rate. Netting these, 15% for Yes sits just below the market anchor and above the structural base rate, which best reflects an entrenched incumbent facing genuine but institutionally unchanneled pressure.

Will Gukesh Dommaraju win the 2026 World.rationale: The match is confirmed and concludes well before the resolution deadline, so this is a clean binary between a slumping reigning champion (2703, rank 31, last place at Chennai Masters) and an in-form challenger (2025 World Cup + record-setting Candidates win). The Polymarket anchor of 30.5% is the only pricing signal, but it is thin (~$37.6k) and un-de-vigged, so it deserves modest rather than absolute deference. The critique is right that the ~69% historical defense base rate, match-play prep dynamics (open-tournament form is a noisier predictor than match preparation), Gukesh's demonstrated match toughness in 2024, and the real possibility of a 7-7 tiebreak all argue for nudging above the market rather than merely matching it. Still, an implied rating gap of roughly 50-60 points plus clear momentum toward Sindarov keeps 'No' the favored bucket. I settle at 34% Yes, slightly above both forecasters and the market.

Will any country expel an Israeli ambass.rationale: The cross-listed Polymarket price (15%, down from 58%) remains the best anchor, and it tracks genuine de-escalation: Colombia restored ties and accepted a new Israeli ambassador, Venezuela normalized after 17 years, and Slovenia reversed course to host Israel's first embassy — shrinking the pool of hostile states that even have a sitting Israeli ambassador to expel (Turkey, South Africa, Ireland already lack one). The Poisson base-rate estimate of 50-65% is materially overstated because it ignores both the market-creation cutoff (South Africa's Jan 2026 chargé d'affaires expulsion likely non-qualifying) and the structural depletion of eligible countries, but the critique is right that a purely mechanical anchor-match under-weights residual risk. I therefore nudge slightly above the anchor to account for: ~4 unobserved months of a fragile ceasefire plus West Bank annexation dynamics, thin market liquidity (~$42.5K) that could leave the price stale, resolution ambiguity around chargé d'affaires-level PNG actions, and under-considered candidates like Chile. Final: Yes 17%, No 83%.

Will Meta be the #2 AI lab at the end of.rationale: The substantive evidence is one-directional: every qualitative source places Anthropic (Opus 5), OpenAI, and Google in the top cluster on LMArena Text Arena Overall, with Meta explicitly outside the leading group; Meta's 2026 flagship (Muse Spark / Spark 1.1 / Glimmer) is characterized as efficiency-focused and sub-frontier, and Llama 5 has slipped to 2027, leaving no plausible frontier release before the Aug 31, 2026 close. Against that, the only live price is a thin Polymarket quote at 91% YES that surged +55pp in 30 days on ~$17K notional — a move too large to dismiss entirely, since resolution is imminent rather than months away and a genuine leaderboard change (or a 'Lab Rank' aggregation quirk / statistical-tie methodology) could explain it. Because the brief has no true Kalshi anchor and no hard Elo snapshot, I take the critique seriously and shade Yes above both forecasters, treating roughly a one-in-five chance that the price surge encodes real information the narrative sources missed. Net: heavily favor No, but with wider tail respect for the market signal than either base forecast allowed.

Another NATO Article 4 invocation by Aug.rationale: The market anchor (8% YES, down from an 18% 30-day high) and the Poisson blend (~7-12% for a ~19-day window) both point strongly to No. The single most informative datapoint is that NATO's August 12 NAC response to a suspected cruise missile 50km inside Poland and repeated drone shoot-downs over Romania was deliberately framed as a solidarity/condemnation statement rather than an Article 4 consultation — evidence that repeated incursions have been normalized and the trigger bar has risen since September 2025. The critique fairly notes that the remaining window matches the Sept 2025 incident-to-invocation lag, that thin volume ($140k) makes the price partly stale, and that any single member (Poland or Romania) can unilaterally trigger consultations — so I nudge modestly above the 8% anchor rather than below it. I do not go near the elevated-tension 26% estimate because that regime parameter is fit to a period when invocations actually occurred, whereas 2026's observed behavior (zero invocations across eight months of comparable incidents) is direct evidence against it. Final: Yes 10%, No 90%.

Israel x Lebanon diplomatic meeting by A.rationale: The Polymarket anchor (~12%) reflects the Aug 6 Rome round ending with no 8th-round date, Hezbollah's Aug 9 boycott push, and a JPost report that continuation slips to September — all pointing to NO within the remaining ~2-3 weeks. However, the critique correctly flags two under-weighted upside factors: the historical cadence of roughly one round every 5-6 weeks (which mean-reverts after prior stalls) is far above the Poisson rate assumed in the brief, and the loose 'direct or via authorized mediator' wording plus the continuous Naqoura five-country mechanism could make a qualifying contact easier than the high-level-round framing implies. The thin, volatile market (6 data points, 24%→7.75%→12%) is a weak anchor that itself signals resolution-criteria uncertainty, warranting a wider band rather than tight anchoring. I therefore set YES modestly above both prior forecasts and the market at 16%, while keeping NO dominant given the explicit suspension and domestic Lebanese political blockage.

Will Russia capture Kostyantynivka by De.rationale: The Polymarket anchor (86.75%, down from 94.75%) is the only usable price, but its downward trend, the independent FutureSearch estimate of 75%, and the documented deceleration (July 2026 regional gains ~27% of July 2025's, ISW reporting 'no confirmed advances' near Kostyantynivka-Druzhkivka, ~50m/day, 8:1 casualty ratio) all point the same direction, justifying a larger haircut than either forecaster applied. The critique is right that the ceasefire pathway is roughly neutral-to-No (a freeze most likely locks in Ukrainian control of the station, since Zelensky has rejected fortress-belt withdrawal), and that in Bakhmut/Avdiivka the key urban core fell only in the final weeks — station capture is plausibly the last domino, not an early one. Autumn mud season and winter further compress the effective offensive window in the ~5 remaining months, and resolution ambiguity (contested Kremlin claims already rejected twice) modestly favors No. Still, Russia holds 37-50% of the city, has made it the top 2026 Donetsk priority, the defending population has collapsed to ~2,800, and the resolution bar is lenient (station-icon shading only), so Yes remains clearly the modal outcome at ~78%.

Will the Democrats win the Iowa Senate r.rationale: The best available market anchor (Polymarket, 43.5% YES with a modest pro-Dem drift and a stable 37.5-46% range) sits meaningfully above a fundamentals model (~25-30%) and roughly at/above Cook's 'Lean Republican' implied ~30-35% for the underdog; the market likely captures real-time campaign dynamics (candidate quality, tightening polls, national environment) that a static model cannot, so I discount the market only modestly rather than splitting the difference. Countervailing structural factors are real and persistent: Iowa has run ~R+10-11 relative to the national environment in each of the last three cycles, no Democrat has won a Senate seat there since 2008, Republicans hold a ~2:1 outside-spending edge, and Iowa polling has historically underestimated Republicans (notably 2020 and 2024). The 2025 special-election closeness and D+5-8 generic ballot are genuine upside signals for Turek but are already substantially priced in, as evidenced by the market trading ~15 points above the fundamentals estimate. Treating the single Emerson +3 poll as decisive would be overreach given sparse polling, so I weight the polling average as roughly a toss-up-to-slight-R lead in a state that typically breaks R late. Final: 40% Yes, a small discount to the market anchor reflecting structural lean and late GOP spending consolidation.

Another Frontier Math Problem Solved by.rationale: The Polymarket mirror at ~91% with a 41-point surge coinciding exactly with Epoch's 8/11 (M23, human-credited) and 8/12 (Hadamard-668, AI-credited provisional) classification updates strongly implies the triggering event has already occurred post-creation, which dominates the pure Poisson base rate (20-63%) that ignores realized events. The critique's strongest points — reversibility of Epoch classifications (the March Ramsey-hypergraph solve was delisted), the explicitly provisional Hadamard status, and unconfirmed market-creation timing — justify shading modestly below the anchor rather than a large discount, since even under a full discount of the August events there remains a ~1.5-month window with an active Book Ramsey candidate under author review, a newly expanded 50-problem surface area, and accelerating AI-math cadence. Thin volume ($15K, 6 days) argues for humility, but the price direction is corroborated by independently documented Epoch page updates, not just trader sentiment. I settle at 0.89 Yes, just below the consensus midpoint and the market anchor, reflecting genuine but bounded resolution-criteria and reversal risk.

Will Ukraine recapture Crimean territory.rationale: ISW has shaded zero Crimean territory as Ukrainian-controlled across ~46 months of war, the front line sits hundreds of kilometers from the isthmus, and Russia retains the full Kherson–Zaporizhzhia land bridge; Ukraine's 2026 Crimea activity (Balaklava, Saky, shadow-fleet tankers) is degradation-by-strike, not ground seizure. Active US-brokered frameworks trend toward Ukraine ceding or freezing Crimea, making the negotiated pathway to qualifying Ukrainian control very thin, and any 'gray zone' deal outcome would be unlikely to produce blue ISW shading persisting two update cycles. I give the critique partial weight — the raid-persistence tail and ISW-interpretation ambiguity are real — but the scenario tree's ~10-12% central estimate looks generous relative to a market that has settled at 6.5-8% on $2.57M volume and to the shrinking remaining window in 2026. I therefore land just below the Polymarket anchor at 5% for Yes, between the two forecasters, reflecting the strict resolution criterion and the very short time left rather than a claim of superior information over the market.

Will Trump visit North Korea by December.rationale: The only direct anchor is Polymarket's identical question at ~7.7% (mildly rising, ~$99K volume), and both forecasters landed just around it, which seems right. The bear case is strong: no invitation, no scheduled Korea travel, Kim's denuclearization redline unresolved, the Oct 2025 APEC/DMZ window explicitly passed, and any late-2026 summit would still need to include physical entry into DPRK territory (a third-country venue or south-side Panmunjom meeting would not resolve YES), a compounding conditional. The critique's strongest point is that the 2019 DMZ crossing itself was improvised with ~24 hours' notice, so long lead time is not strictly required — this offsets the downward shading Forecast 1 applied and argues against going below the market. Balancing the compressed post-midterm window and White House 'talks moving quickly' chatter (upside) against the strict physical-entry bar (downside), I settle essentially at the market anchor, ~7%.

Will any country expel a U.S. ambassador.rationale: Both forecasters converge just below the thin Polymarket anchor (15.5%), and the core structural argument is sound: the most hostile counterparties (Venezuela, Colombia, Honduras, Brazil) currently lack Senate-confirmed U.S. ambassadors in post, so they cannot generate a qualifying event, and the only live threat — a Canadian citizen petition against Hoekstra — has not been endorsed by the Carney government and would be an unprecedented move by a G7 ally. The critique fairly notes that the qualifying space is broader (PNG declarations count, not just formal expulsions), that 2026 resembles a clustering period of regional diplomatic volatility, and that a Brazil confirmation could reopen risk — these argue against pushing far below the market. Countering that, only ~4.5 months remain from the research cutoff to close, and no official government-level threat exists, which supports shading modestly below 15.5%. I settle at 12% Yes, slightly below the anchor but above Forecast 1, with reduced confidence given thin liquidity and no direct Kalshi price.

Will Russia capture Prymorske by Decembe.rationale: The Polymarket anchor of 17.5% (flat recently, down from a 37.5% peak) reflects a market that has watched eight-plus months of failed Russian assaults on this micro-target and repriced toward stalemate. Confirmed reporting through Aug 9, 2026 shows Prymorske as a gray zone with Russia having lost its southern foothold, Ukraine retaking adjacent Stepnohirsk, and no ISW-red shading — the specific resolution criterion is stricter than mere infiltration, which is exactly why generic advance-rate Monte Carlo models (~56%) and the 30-55% reference class overstate YES here. The devil's advocate is right that ~4.5 months of unknown developments remain and that a renewed Russian push after Ukrainian counteroffensive momentum fades is a real path, so I nudge marginally above the anchor rather than below it, but the documented local reversal is genuinely diagnostic and justifies sitting below the generic reference class. Stalled negotiations (Russia rejecting a line-freeze) make a settlement-based transfer of control unlikely, and any ambiguous freeze scenario would more likely fail the strict ISW-shading criterion than satisfy it. Final: 18% Yes.

Total Internet Blackout in Iran by Augus.rationale: With only ~2 weeks left in the window and connectivity restored since May 26 (~86%), the pure base-rate hazard (~3.6%/month) implies ~2% residual risk, while the Polymarket anchor of 7.5% likely embeds both a wider remaining window at the time of pricing and momentum effects on thin volume. Will Russia capture Orikhiv by September.rationale: The same-event Polymarket price of 7.35% (flat, near its historical low) is the strongest anchor, and ISW as of mid-August 2026 confirms only infiltration attempts at Orikhiv's southern edge while explicitly rejecting milblogger encirclement claims. The resolution bar — ISW red shading at the train station persisting a full update cycle — is materially stricter than infiltration reporting, and theater/sector advance rates have been flat since February with prior assaults 'virtually halted' and Mala Tokmachka retaken in May. Will Trump meet with Volodymyr Zelenskyy.rationale: The live market anchor (7.5%, trending down from 14.5%) is the best real-time evidence that no Trump–Zelenskyy meeting is currently scheduled for August 2026, and no source reports any announced bilateral or multilateral event for the month. However, the critique is partly right that both forecasters leaned too heavily on a thin ($105K) market and on weakly relevant Putin–Zelenskyy cross-market signals, while the empirical cadence (7-8 meetings since Jan 2025, ~50-65% monthly recently, including an Aug 2025 precedent) and the live Patriot/peace-talks agenda create genuine ad-hoc meeting risk over the ~25 remaining unobserved days. Will Ukraine re-enter Rodynske by Septem.rationale: All August 2026 reporting converges on Russian consolidation of Rodynske, with the battle assessed 'effectively over' and active fighting shifted west toward Dobropillya/Shevchenko; the settlement pathway points toward Ukraine ceding Donbas, not regaining it, so it adds negligible YES mass. The critique's strongest point cuts both ways: the persistence requirement makes brief infiltrations less likely to resolve YES, but ISW occasionally shades short-lived Ukrainian infiltration (as in Nov 2025), and a second-order effect from Ukrainian activity near Dobropillya is a small live pathway — these roughly offset. With ~7 weeks to the deadline and momentum firmly against Ukraine in this sector, I settle just below the proxy anchor at 8% rather than the 7% low end, reflecting the thinner-than-implied evidence base.

NATO downs another Russian drone by Augu.rationale: The Polymarket-mirrored anchor of 63% (rising sharply after the Aug 14 Latvia shootdown) is consistent with a Poisson model on the recent tempo (~4 qualifying incidents in 8 weeks, i.e., ~1.3-2/month) over the remaining ~2.5-week window, which yields P(≥1) ≈ 55-70%. The critique's strongest point cuts upward: if market creation was in late July, the confirmed Aug 14 Italian Eurofighter shootdown over Latvia may already satisfy resolution, giving a non-trivial chance the question is effectively pre-resolved YES. Offsetting downside risks — attribution ambiguity (several incidents were EW-redirected Ukrainian drones, contested as 'Russian'), regression to mean if the Jun-Aug cluster was a temporary campaign, and the reference-class mismatch of the IISS detection count — justify not moving far above the anchor. Iran charges Hormuz fees by August 31?.rationale: The resolution bar requires both an official Iranian announcement and consensus reporting that mandatory collection has actually begun — as of mid-August only a Majlis committee-approved draft framework (Aug 9) exists, and the Strait is largely closed with traffic collapsed after the Aug 14 ADNOC attacks. Against that, IMO/UNCLOS opposition, unified shipping-industry and US pushback, Iran's July 28 rejection of Oman's plan, and the sharp market de-risking from 51.5% to 9.5% all support No, and 'consensus reporting that collection has begun' is a demanding standard amid a wartime information environment. Maduro guilty of all counts?.rationale: The binding constraint is timing, not conviction propensity: a June 1, 2027 trial start leaves roughly seven months of slack, and complex SDNY narco-trials (El Chapo ~12 weeks plus deliberation) combined with routine continuances, the unresolved sovereign-immunity motion argued Nov 17, 2026, and hung-jury/retrial risk make a completed all-counts verdict before Dec 31, 2027 far from assured. Decomposing explicitly — P(verdict rendered by deadline) roughly 0.35–0.45 given continuance and mistrial risk, times P(guilty on all four counts | verdict) roughly 0.70–0.80 (the 4/4 comparable base rate is strong but the sample is small, self-selected, and none involved a head of state with novel immunity/political defenses, and the machine-gun counts are the most plausible partial-acquittal vector) — yields the high-20s. The critique's point that partial dismissal of counts is an additional distinct pathway to No, and that retrial after a hung jury compounds rather than substitutes for delay risk, justifies sitting a touch below the 29% Polymarket anchor rather than at or above it. Will the Republican Party hold between 2.rationale: The 220–224 band is a narrow 5-seat window inside a distribution with large residual variance (uncalled toss-ups, Maryland amendment, unresolved maps), so even if the center of the distribution were exactly 222, this bucket would capture only ~15-20% of mass; but the center is likely lower. Will the minimum Arctic sea ice extent t.rationale: Only 2 of the last 19 years (2012's cyclone-driven 3.39M and 2020's 3.74M) finished below 4.0M km², giving a ~10% empirical base rate, while a trend+residual normal model gives ~19%; the reasonable blend sits near 12-15%. Will Nicolás Maduro be sentenced to no p.rationale: The resolution rule is decisive: any outcome other than an actual custodial sentence imposed by Dec 31, 2027 — including a case still pending — resolves Yes. The critique is right that an internal STF rupture and a possible multi-front crisis (renewed US sanctions, Senate friction, editorial pressure) create genuine tail risk for a negotiated exit or resignation, so I keep meaningful mass on Yes rather than collapsing to the structural base rate. Netting these, I land at 17% YES, between the two forecasts and well below the market.

Will OpenAI’s Astra model debut on the A.rationale: No Kalshi price exists, so the Polymarket proxy at 65.5% YES is the best anchor, but its steep 30-day slide from 81.5% coinciding with the Critical-cybersecurity gating is a real signal that traders are pricing a non-trivial chance Astra never gets a standard crowd-sourced Arena listing before close, or lands below the frontier cluster. Decomposing: conditional on a listing, Astra being rated roughly equal to Fable 5 while the top cluster sits at 1500-1525 gives perhaps ~75-80% odds of clearing 1480, tempered by felloai indices showing it tying or trailing rivals on preference-relevant measures; the listing itself is likely but not assured given the gated rollout. The historical 'new #1 debuts +20 pts' pattern is weakly sourced and should not be leaned on heavily. Netting a ~80% clearance probability against ~80% listing probability lands near the anchor, and the bearish momentum plus unresolved gaps justify a modest tilt below it to 0.62.

Will Jared Kushner attend a US x Iran di.rationale: Both forecasters landed at 18% by shading slightly below the Polymarket proxy (20%), and the critique correctly notes neither decomposed the compound condition. Doing so roughly: P(a qualifying senior round occurs by Dec 31) ~40-45% given the 3-4 month historical cadence, four months remaining, and the pattern of sanctions pressure preceding talks despite Trump's public denials; P(Kushner attends | round) ~45-50% given he is a named member of the Witkoff-Vance-Kushner trio with Geneva precedent but was not confirmed at the June round, Iran reportedly prefers Vance, and his bandwidth is on Gaza/Ukraine. That yields ~18-22%, consistent with the thin Polymarket anchor rather than justifying a shade below it. The critique's bullish points (Kushner's own 'robust contacts' claim, pressure-then-talks cycle) roughly offset the negative trajectory, so I set YES at 20%.

Will OpenAI announce another Millennium.rationale: Both forecasters independently landed at 8%, and the critique's points largely offset: competitive pressure with Anthropic and OpenAI's demonstrated ability to mobilize agent swarms in days raise the tail (a rushed, loosely-verified 'solved' claim would count under the market's no-Clay-verification standard), while the reference class (one Millennium Problem solved in 24 years) and the complete absence of any identified OpenAI program on Riemann/P vs NP/Yang-Mills/Hodge/BSD push lower. The ~3-week window, OpenAI's stated pivot to room-temperature superconductivity, and its bandwidth being absorbed defending the disputed Navier-Stokes priority claim all argue the thin, hype-inflated 14.5% Polymarket price overstates YES. The Navier-Stokes precedent shows a Millennium-level attempt can go from start to announcement in ~7 days, so a non-trivial tail remains, but the remaining problems are materially harder with no visible groundwork. I settle slightly below the consensus at 7%.

2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House.rationale: Both forecasts converge on the Polymarket anchor (13.5%) and the Kalshi Speaker market (Jeffries 87%), and the critique does not overturn this. The brief's copula estimate of 19-35% rests on P(R Senate)≈0.75-0.85, which contradicts Silver's FLIPR (R Senate 43%), so that upward signal is unreliable; conversely, the proper decomposition P(R House)≈0.13 × P(R Senate | R House)≈0.85-0.90 yields ~0.11-0.12, consistent with the market. A D+7 generic ballot, Trump net approval near -20 or worse, and a razor-thin GOP House majority make the House hold the binding constraint, while polling-miss tail risk and pending redistricting litigation keep a real but modest upset path alive. The stressed historical retention rate (~25%) is a loose upper reference given this cycle's unusually severe environment. I settle at 13% YES, in line with the market and both forecasters.

Will Russia enter Stavky by September 30.rationale: Both forecasters drew the same inference from the sub-questions: no qualifying shading in Stavky, Ukrainian counterattacks and troop buildup in the village itself as of Sept 7-8, a glacial front-wide Russian advance (~124 km² in August), and no ceasefire path that would cede the village — all pointing to No with roughly three weeks remaining. However, the infiltration-shading tail path is weakened by evidence that current infiltration momentum in this sector favors Ukraine, and the Monte Carlo range predates confirmation of the reversed salient, so it deserves heavy discounting. I settle at 19% YES, below the 28.5% proxy anchor but not below the forecasters' range, reflecting Russia's historical March proximity to Drobysheve/Lyman and the unknown current frontline distance.
