That multiplies to ~7-10%, consistent with both forecasters and above the quant model's 2% point estimate. The critique is right that the rising Polymarket price (14%) shouldn't be dismissed outright, but thin volume and the tendency of long-dated binaries to overprice tail YES justify a modest discount rather than full adoption. Resolution uses the prospectus IPO price, not first-day pop, so debut surges don't help Yes. Final: 10% Yes, 90% No.

The unsourced Wikipedia 'captured 23 July' claim is contradicted by the market's decline and by continued reports of fighting in and around Bilytske, so I discount it heavily while leaving some tail mass for ISW assessment lag. I hold at the market anchor with a minimal nudge for Russian momentum on the Dobropillia axis.

Will S&P 500 (SPX) hit $5,200 (LOW) in D.rationale: SPX at 7,591.70 on 2026-09-09 needs a ~31.5% decline to touch 5,200, and since no touch has occurred to date only ~3.7 months of the window remain; a crash of that size in under four months from near all-time highs has happened only a handful of times in a century (1929, 1987, 2020), so the ~3% 12-month base rate itself overstates the relevant odds. Macro gauges (positive 2s10s, HY OAS ~2.7%, VIX ~16, Fed steady) show no crisis mechanism, and even the most bearish major-bank target (BofA 7,100) sits ~37% above the strike. The critique's points about the live US-Iran war/oil shock and analysts' systematic underweighting of tails are valid and justify staying above the pure base rate, but they do not overcome the short remaining horizon; the Polymarket 7% anchor is thin and likely carries longshot bias, and its 18.5% high plausibly dates to when spot was lower. I land between the two forecasts at ~4% YES.

Will the peak RONI for the 2026–27 El Ni.rationale: The most on-topic anchor is CPC's own August estimate of 69% that OND 2026 RONI reaches ≥2.5°C, and since this market resolves on the peak across ASO–DJF (strictly more permissive than OND alone), that figure argues for something at or above ~69%; conditions have only strengthened since (very-strong odds rose from 81% to >90%, exceptional >8°C subsurface anomalies, continued WWBs). The critique is right that the historical base rate is largely priced into CPC's model rather than being independent bearish evidence, so I don't double-count it, but the thin, volatile market and stale RONI data warrant staying a few points below the CPC-implied peak probability. I land at 66% Yes, slightly above both forecasters and the market, below CPC's raw figure.

Will Anthropic announce a Millennium Pri.rationale: Both forecasters correctly read the sub-questions: Anthropic's only relevant result is an explicitly partial Riemann bound it said would not lead to a proof, no claims exist on the other qualifying problems, and the only hot rumor concerns Navier-Stokes, which is excluded and was an OpenAI claim anyway. Will the Hodge Conjecture be the next Mi.rationale: The only market anchor is a thin, rumor-driven Polymarket price (41.5% latest vs ~30.5% in an earlier snapshot), so averaging the snapshots and discounting for the uncorroborated Sept 9 X post is appropriate. Hodge has zero confirmed AI progress while Riemann has tangible partial results and BSD was market-favored in one snapshot; P vs NP and Yang-Mills also carry unmodeled mass, and resolution-criteria ambiguity plus the historical base rate argue for a fatter 'no qualifying solution' bucket. Offsetting this, labs (especially OpenAI, with its 10,000-agent Navier-Stokes effort) have shown they will announce contested 'solutions' quickly, the bar is a lab announcement rather than Clay verification, and the specific Hodge rumor plausibly reflects real OpenAI interest that the market is pricing. Both forecasters drew the same inference and the critique mostly reinforces shading below the headline price rather than exposing a shared flaw, so I settle at 0.32, between the two forecasts and below the latest market print.

Will Erling Haaland be the #1 searched p.rationale: The best available anchor is Polymarket's 19% YES price, and both forecasters shaded slightly below it citing the historical pattern that Year in Search People winners are usually driven by acute late-year shock events (Depp, Hamlin, D4vd, Kobe) and that no footballer topped the global list in prior World Cup years (2018, 2022). Will Moonshot be the second-best Chinese.rationale: Qwen is the settled #1 Chinese lab, so this reduces to whether Moonshot's Kimi K3 lands exactly at #2 ahead of Z.ai (GLM-5.3), DeepSeek (V4 family), and secondary entrants (Tencent Hunyuan, Xiaomi, MiniMax) on the overall style-control-off Text Arena on Oct 31. Counterweights are that the K2 'tied 8th' snapshot predates K3, K3 has real frontier momentum, and the thin Polymarket price (44.5%, drifting up) likely reflects participants who can see the live board. Volatility through October cuts both ways and does not justify a large move from the anchor. Will Likud win fewer than 20 seats in th.rationale: Both forecasters anchor on the ~14.8% market price, which is consistent with a poll cluster of 22-27 seats, a ~9% historical base rate for Likud falling below 20, and Likud's tendency to consolidate right-wing votes late and slightly outperform polls. Legacy's undefeated group run (including a 2-0 over pre-event favorite FURIA), #8 ranking, HLTV's 'most consistent team' framing, absence of all elite teams, and a thin but rising market all justify a slight lean above the anchor.
